lanes.label: Version 1 · new numbers
lanes.stem: A marine biologist conducts a study to determine if a new water filtration system alters the average salinity level of a coastal habitat relative to a historical baseline. The statistical analysis yields a p-value of 0.012 at a significance threshold of alpha = 0.05. Which of the following is the correct interpretation of this p-value?

lanes.label: Version 2 · real-world setting
lanes.stem: A marine biology lab tests whether a new fertilizer formulation alters the average daily growth rate of a cultured kelp species. After running a trial with 40 culture tanks, the data analyst reports a p-value of 0.018 for the two-tailed hypothesis test. How should the lab's lead scientist correctly interpret this result?

lanes.label: Version 3 · what-if
lanes.stem: A clinical trial yields an observed test statistic corresponding to a two-tailed p-value of 0.08 (an 8% chance of observing data at least this extreme in either direction under the null hypothesis). Consider a counterfactual scenario where the study had instead specified a one-tailed test in the direction of the observed data prior to data collection, resulting in a halved p-value of 0.04. What is the correct interpretation of this counterfactual 0.04 p-value?
